data.headline: PSO clears air about its investment in PRL
data.summary: PSO has clarified that its investment worth USD 1.5-2bn through debt in PRL REUP is still at a premature stage and nothing conclusive or definitive has taken place.

data.headline: USD 10bn green refinery SIFC asks MoFA to take Sinopec, Aramco on board for MoU with PSO
data.summary: Pakistan wants the state-owned PSO Chinese Sinopec and Saudi Aramco to sign a non-binding MoU for materializing the USD 10bn green refinery. The SIFC to this effect has directed the MoFA to facilitate the Petroleum Division to take Saudi Aramco and Sinopec on board for signing a non-binding trilateral MoU with PSO for cooperation on the green refinery project, a senior SIFC official told The News.

data.headline: PSO receivables hit PKR 810bn mark
data.summary: The total receivables of PSO have reached PKR 810bn, however the management indicated that due to the significant increase in consumer gas prices, PSO’s liquidity position is anticipated to improve.

data.headline: PSO proposes debt swap for equity in companies
data.summary: Pakistan State Oil, the country’s largest oil marketer, says it is in talks with the government on a plan to acquire stakes in public sector energy companies and offset mounting debt it is owed by firms such as the national airline.

data.headline: PSO receivables mount to PKR 804.5bn by March closure
data.summary: Pakistan State Oil (PSO), the state-controlled oil marketing firm, is wrestling with an alarming financial crunch as its receivables have ballooned to over PKR 800 bn by March end, exacerbated by delayed payments from both public and private sectors.

data.headline: PSO ramps up diesel imports ahead of harvest season
data.summary: Pakistan State Oil (PSO), the country's top oil marketing company, has placed substantial orders for diesel imports in anticipation of the agricultural harvesting season, industry officials said on Wednesday.

data.headline: PSO receiveables soar to PKR21.7bn
data.summary: The Pakistan State Oil (PSO) has proposed the imposition of a levy of upto PKR 4 per litre on Jet-A1 to recover outstanding receivables from Pakistan International Airlines (PIA).

data.headline: PSO to write letter to govt to help the entity avert default
data.summary: Chairman Board of Management (BoM) of Pakistan State Oil (PSO), Asif Baig Mohamed will write a SOS (Save Our Ship) letter to the federal government for immediate payment of PKR 70bn to the company to avert imminent default.
